1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.g3.strategy: The standard set-up: White prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop, aiming it down the long diagonal at the e4 square Black's f-pawn tries to control. It is a flexible, solid plan that keeps the king safe and lets White choose when to challenge the centre.
1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.g3.name: Dutch Defence: Fianchetto Variation

1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.Nc3.strategy: Develops the knight to its most active square, adding to the pressure on e4 and d5 so that a later e2-e4 strike has support. The bishop on f1 stays at home for now, so White keeps a choice between a fianchetto and a more direct central game.
1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.Nc3.name: Dutch Defence: Queen's Knight Variation

1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.g3 e6.strategy: Props up the f5 pawn, guards d5 and opens the diagonal for the king's bishop, preparing a solid set-up with castling to follow. The price is a closed game: the light-squared bishop stays shut in behind its own pawns until the d-pawn moves.

1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.g3 g6.strategy: Prepares to fianchetto the king's bishop: it will guard the king and press on the long diagonal. The cost is a looser kingside, which Black accepts for active piece play.

1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.g3 d6.strategy: A flexible but modest move: it takes e5 under pawn control and frees the c8-bishop to defend f5, while leaving open how Black arranges the kingside. It does little else, and White completes the fianchetto and castles at leisure.

1.d4 f5 2.c4 Nf6 3.Nc3 d6.strategy: A solid, flexible reply: the pawn takes e5 and c5 under control and frees the c8-bishop to defend f5. Black keeps the kingside set-up open for later, and meets White's pressure on e4 calmly.
